{{Short description|French chemist (born 1948)}}
'''Michel Rohmer''', born on 31 January 1948, is a French [[chemist]] specialising in the chemistry of [[Microorganism|micro-organisms]]. He has particularly studied [[isoprenoids]].

He is a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences|French Academy of sciences]].

== Biography ==
Michel Rohmer studied at the École nationale supérieure de chimie in [[Strasbourg]]. He defended his thesis at the [[Louis Pasteur University|Louis-Pasteur University]] in Strasbourg in 1975 in [[Guy Ourisson]]'s laboratory. He became professor of organic and bio-organic chemistry at the [[École nationale supérieure de chimie de Mulhouse]] from 1979 to 1994, then returned to the Université Louis-Pasteur in Strasbourg. He was Director of the Institut de chimie de Strasbourg (UMR 7177).<ref>{{cite web|title=Faculté de Chimie: Accueil - Université de Strasbourg|url=http://chimie.unistra.fr/|website=chimie.unistra.fr|access-date=2019-02-21}}</ref> Since 1 September 2013, he has been Professor Emeritus of the [[University of Strasbourg]].

== Research ==
Michel Rohmer is working on isoprenoids, a class of natural substances familiar to all in the form of [[cholesterol]] in our cells. He studied [[hopanoids]] in particular, which are found in sedimentary rock materials. He then discovered biohopanoids, a family of pentacyclic [[Triterpene|triterpenoids]]. His work on the biosynthesis of these bacterial hopanoids is revolutionizing the understanding of the early stages of isoprenoid biosynthesis. Rohmer proposes a new biosynthetic pathway leading to the universal precursors of isoprenoids, [[isopentenyl]] and [[Dimethylallyl-diphosphate:isopentenyl-diphosphate dimethylallyltranstransferase|dimethylallyl diphosphates]]. This path is different from the [[mevalonate]] path that has been accepted for more than fifty years. The metabolic pathway of [[methylerythritol phosphate]] is widely distributed in bacteria, which are omnipresent in the [[chloroplast]]s of [[phototroph]]ic organisms.

== Awards and honours ==

*    Valiant Prize of the French Academy of sciences (1984)
*    Gold medal of the Wallach Foundation, Mulhouse (1993)
*    Franco-British Prize of the [[Royal Society]] and the French Academy of sciences (1993)
*    Gay-Lussac Humboldt Prize of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] (1997<ref>{{Cite web| title=Liste des lauréats français du prix Gay-Lussac Humbold | language=fr | trans-title=List of French winners of the Gay-Lussac Humboldt Prize | url=http://media.education.gouv.fr/file/Brochures/77/6/listelaureatsall12-2_25776.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726134631/http://media.education.gouv.fr/file/Brochures/77/6/listelaureatsall12-2_25776.pdf | archive-date=2011-07-26}}</ref>)
*    Member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France|Institut universitaire de France]] (1997)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://iuf.amue.fr/author/mrohmer/ |title=IUF » Michel ROHMER |access-date=2019-11-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081126034314/http://iuf.amue.fr/author/mrohmer/ |archive-date=2008-11-26 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*    Member of the German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina (2000)
*    Member of the French Academy of sciences (elected Correspondent on 15 April 1996 and Member on 18 November 2003)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/membres/R/Rohmer_Michel_bio.htm |title=Michel Rohmer : Repères biographiques - les membres de l'Académie des sciences |access-date=2019-11-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090529055258/http://www.academie-sciences.fr/Membres/R/Rohmer_Michel_bio.htm |archive-date=2009-05-29 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*    Nakanishi Prize, Japan Chemical Society and [[American Chemical Society]] (2008)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en.html|title=American Chemical Society|website=American Chemical Society}}</ref>
*    Schroepfer Award, [[American Oil Chemists' Society|American Oil Chemists Society]] (2008)
*    Albert Hofmann Award, [[University of Zurich]], Switzerland (2008)
